content.title: About
content.content: Pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) is a marine fish from the jack family, native to warm coastal waters of the Indo‑Pacific region. Fried pompano has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a crispy crust that keeps the flesh moist.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden fish” because of its golden‑hued flesh.
The species grows quickly, reaching up to 30 cm in its first year.
In Japan, pompano is considered a delicacy and appears in high‑end sushi menus.
High‑heat frying preserves most of the omega‑3 fatty acids that are heart‑healthy.
Pompano adapts well to aquaculture, making it widely available worldwide.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health and help reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Provides all essential amino acids, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D is important for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and iodine
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, while iodine supports thyroid function.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, pompano contains less mercury, making it a safer frequent choice.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: High sodium if heavily salted
items.content: Excess salt during frying can increase cardiovascular strain.

items.title: Trans fats from improper frying
items.content: Overheating oil creates trans fats, which are detrimental to health.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Fried fish is calorie‑dense; moderate portions help prevent weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pompano can be served as a standalone main, sliced into salads, used in tacos, or as a sandwich filling. A squeeze of lemon, fresh herbs, and a light sauce enhance its flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fried pompano in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness before serving.
